description.it: Creare un ConfigMap con dati di configurazione
description.en: Create a ConfigMap with configuration data

exercises.task:
1. Crea un ConfigMap chiamato 'app-config'
2. Includi chiavi: DB_HOST=db.example.com, DB_PORT=5432
3. Verifica che sia stato creato correttamente
4. Controlla i dettagli del ConfigMap
hints: kubectl get configmaps per vedere la lista
exercises.solution:
kubectl create configmap app-config --from-literal=DB_HOST=db.example.com --from-literal=DB_PORT=5432
kubectl get configmap app-config
kubectl describe configmap app-config

description.it: Iniettare valori del ConfigMap in un Pod
description.en: Inject ConfigMap values into a Pod

exercises.task:
1. Crea un Pod 'config-pod' con immagine busybox
2. Imposta variabili d'ambiente DB_HOST e DB_PORT dal ConfigMap 'app-config'
3. Esegui il comando: env
4. Verifica che le variabili siano impostate
hints: Specifica il nome del ConfigMap con name
exercises.solution:
kubectl apply -f - << 'EOF'
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: config-pod
spec:
  containers:
  - name: test
    image: busybox
    command: ['sh', '-c', 'env && sleep 3600']
    env:
    - name: DB_HOST
      valueFrom:
        configMapKeyRef:
          name: app-config
          key: DB_HOST
    - name: DB_PORT
      valueFrom:
        configMapKeyRef:
          name: app-config
          key: DB_PORT
EOF

kubectl wait --for=condition=Ready pod/config-pod --timeout=30s
kubectl exec config-pod -- env | grep DB
exercises.validation: kubectl exec config-pod -- env | grep DB_HOST

title.it: Caricare tutto un ConfigMap con envFrom

description.it: Iniettare tutte le chiavi di un ConfigMap

exercises.task:
1. Crea un Pod 'envfrom-pod' con immagine busybox
2. Carica tutto il ConfigMap 'app-config' con envFrom
3. Verifica che tutte le variabili siano presenti
4. Controlla che non ci siano conflitti
hints: envFrom configura un blocco di variabili
exercises.solution:
kubectl apply -f - << 'EOF'
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: envfrom-pod
spec:
  containers:
  - name: test
    image: busybox
    command: ['sh', '-c', 'env | sort && sleep 3600']
    envFrom:
    - configMapRef:
        name: app-config
EOF

kubectl wait --for=condition=Ready pod/envfrom-pod --timeout=30s
kubectl exec envfrom-pod -- env | grep -E 'DB_HOST|DB_PORT'

exercises.task:
1. Crea un ConfigMap 'nginx-config' con nginx.conf
2. Montalo in /etc/nginx/conf.d/ in un Pod nginx
3. Verifica che il file sia presente
4. Controlla che sia read-only
exercises.solution:
echo 'server { listen 8080; }' > nginx.conf
kubectl create configmap nginx-config --from-file=nginx.conf

kubectl apply -f - << 'EOF'
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: nginx-config-pod
spec:
  containers:
  - name: nginx
    image: nginx:alpine
    volumeMounts:
    - name: config
      mountPath: /etc/nginx/conf.d/nginx.conf
      subPath: nginx.conf
      readOnly: true
  volumes:
  - name: config
    configMap:
      name: nginx-config
EOF

kubectl wait --for=condition=Ready pod/nginx-config-pod --timeout=30s
kubectl exec nginx-config-pod -- cat /etc/nginx/conf.d/nginx.conf
exercises.validation: kubectl exec nginx-config-pod -- ls -la /etc/nginx/conf.d/ | grep nginx.conf

description.it: Esporre metadati del Pod al container
description.en: Expose Pod metadata to the container

exercises.task:
1. Crea un Pod 'downward-pod'
2. Esponi il nome del Pod, namespace e IP come variabili d'ambiente
3. Esponi anche labels come file in un volume
4. Verifica che i valori siano corretti
exercises.solution:
kubectl apply -f - << 'EOF'
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: downward-pod
  labels:
    app: test
spec:
  containers:
  - name: test
    image: busybox
    command: ['sh', '-c', 'env && sleep 3600']
    env:
    - name: POD_NAME
      valueFrom:
        fieldRef:
          fieldPath: metadata.name
    - name: POD_NAMESPACE
      valueFrom:
        fieldRef:
          fieldPath: metadata.namespace
    - name: POD_IP
      valueFrom:
        fieldRef:
          fieldPath: status.podIP
    volumeMounts:
    - name: labels
      mountPath: /etc/labels
  volumes:
  - name: labels
    downwardAPI:
      items:
      - path: "labels"
        fieldRef:
          fieldPath: metadata.labels
EOF

kubectl wait --for=condition=Ready pod/downward-pod --timeout=30s
kubectl exec downward-pod -- env | grep POD
kubectl exec downward-pod -- cat /etc/labels/labels

description.it: Impostare requests e limits per CPU e memoria
description.en: Set requests and limits for CPU and memory

exercises.task:
1. Crea un Pod 'resource-pod'
2. Imposta requests: 100m CPU, 128Mi memoria
3. Imposta limits: 500m CPU, 256Mi memoria
4. Verifica la configurazione
exercises.solution:
kubectl apply -f - << 'EOF'
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: resource-pod
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: nginx:alpine
    resources:
      requests:
        cpu: 100m
        memory: 128Mi
      limits:
        cpu: 500m
        memory: 256Mi
EOF

kubectl describe pod resource-pod | grep -A 5 'Limits\|Requests'

description.it: Impostare default e limiti per namespace
description.en: Set defaults and limits for namespace

exercises.task:
1. Crea un namespace 'limited'
2. Crea un LimitRange con default: 200m CPU, 256Mi memoria
3. Imposta anche max: 1 CPU, 512Mi memoria
4. Testa creando un Pod senza resources specificate
hints: LimitRange applica defaults ai Pod senza resources
Specifica type: Container per limiti ai container
exercises.solution:
kubectl create namespace limited
kubectl apply -n limited -f - << 'EOF'
apiVersion: v1
kind: LimitRange
metadata:
  name: cpu-mem-limit
spec:
  limits:
  - type: Container
    default:          # limits
      cpu: 200m
      memory: 256Mi
    defaultRequest:   # requests
      cpu: 50m
      memory: 64Mi
    max:
      cpu: 1
      memory: 512Mi
EOF

kubectl apply -n limited -f - << 'EOF'
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: test-pod
spec:
  containers:
  - name: nginx
    image: nginx:alpine
EOF

kubectl get -n limited limitrange
kubectl describe -n limited pod test-pod | grep -A 5 'Limits|Requests'
exercises.validation: kubectl get -n limited limitrange cpu-mem-limit -o jsonpath='{.spec.limits[0].default.cpu}'

exercises.task:
1. Crea un ResourceQuota 'compute-quota' nel namespace 'limited'
2. Limita: max 10 Pod, 2 CPU totali, 2Gi memoria totale
3. Verifica che venga applicato
4. Testa il blocco superando i limiti
hints: Specifica hard limits per CPU, memoria, pods
Il blocco avviene alla creazione del Pod
exercises.solution:
kubectl apply -n limited -f - << 'EOF'
apiVersion: v1
kind: ResourceQuota
metadata:
  name: compute-quota
spec:
  hard:
    pods: 10
    requests.cpu: 2
    requests.memory: 2Gi
    limits.cpu: 4
    limits.memory: 4Gi
EOF

kubectl get -n limited resourcequota
kubectl describe -n limited resourcequota compute-quota
exercises.validation: kubectl get -n limited resourcequota compute-quota -o jsonpath='{.spec.hard.pods}'

description.it: Creare classi di priorità per i Pod

exercises.task:
1. Crea una PriorityClass 'high-priority' con valore 1000000
2. Crea una PriorityClass 'low-priority' con valore 100
3. Crea due Pod con diverse priorità
4. Verifica l'ordine di preemption
exercises.solution:
kubectl apply -f - << 'EOF'
apiVersion: scheduling.k8s.io/v1
kind: PriorityClass
metadata:
  name: high-priority
value: 1000000
globalDefault: false
description: "High priority for critical workloads"
---
apiVersion: scheduling.k8s.io/v1
kind: PriorityClass
metadata:
  name: low-priority
value: 100
globalDefault: true
description: "Low priority for batch workloads"
EOF

kubectl get priorityclasses

exercises.task:
1. Crea un Pod con ConfigMap montato come volume
2. Modifica il ConfigMap aggiungendo una nuova chiave
3. Verifica che il file sia aggiornato nel Pod
4. Nota: l'aggiornamento può richiedere tempo
hints: Il sync avviene automaticamente per volumi
Può richiedere fino a 1 minuto per kubelet sync
exercises.solution:
# Crea ConfigMap iniziale
kubectl create configmap dynamic-config --from-literal=KEY1=value1

# Pod con volume
kubectl apply -f - << 'EOF'
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: dynamic-pod
spec:
  containers:
  - name: test
    image: busybox
    command: ['sh', '-c', 'while true; do cat /config/KEY1; sleep 5; done']
    volumeMounts:
    - name: config
      mountPath: /config
  volumes:
  - name: config
    configMap:
      name: dynamic-config
EOF

# Attendi e verifica
kubectl wait --for=condition=Ready pod/dynamic-pod --timeout=30s
kubectl exec dynamic-pod -- cat /config/KEY1

# Aggiorna ConfigMap
kubectl patch configmap dynamic-config --type='json' -p='[{"op": "add", "path": "/data/KEY2", "value": "value2"}]'

# Verifica dopo sync
sleep 10
kubectl exec dynamic-pod -- ls /config/

description.it: Testare il comportamento di memory limit

exercises.task:
1. Crea un Pod con memory limit molto basso (10Mi)
2. Esegui uno script che alloca memoria
3. Osserva il Pod essere terminato con OOMKilled
4. Controlla lo stato del Pod
hints: Usa stress o uno script Python per allocare memoria
Il container verrà terminato, non throttled
exercises.solution:
kubectl apply -f - << 'EOF'
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: oom-test
spec:
  containers:
  - name: stress
    image: progrium/stress
    command: ['stress', '--vm', '1', '--vm-bytes', '20M']
    resources:
      limits:
        memory: 10Mi
EOF

sleep 10
kubectl get pod oom-test -o jsonpath='{.status.containerStatuses[0].lastState.terminated.reason}'
exercises.validation: kubectl describe pod oom-test | grep -i 'OOMKilled\|Exit Code'

exercises.task:
1. Crea un file config.json con configurazione dell'app
2. Crea un ConfigMap 'app-json-config' dal file
3. Montalo come volume nel Pod
4. Verifica che il file JSON sia accessibile
hints: Il nome del file diventa la chiave
Il contenuto del file diventa il valore
exercises.solution:
echo '{"database": {"host": "localhost", "port": 5432}}' > config.json
kubectl create configmap app-json-config --from-file=config.json

kubectl apply -f - << 'EOF'
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: json-pod
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: busybox
    command: ['sh', '-c', 'cat /config/config.json && sleep 3600']
    volumeMounts:
    - name: config
      mountPath: /config
      readOnly: true
  volumes:
  - name: config
    configMap:
      name: app-json-config
EOF

kubectl exec json-pod -- cat /config/config.json

description.it: Osservare il comportamento di CPU limit

exercises.task:
1. Crea un Pod con CPU request 100m e limit 200m
2. Esegui un carico CPU intenso
3. Osserva che il processo viene throttled, non ucciso
4. Misura la CPU effettivamente usata
hints: CPU è comprimibile, viene throttled non ucciso
kubectl top pod per vedere utilizzo
exercises.solution:
kubectl apply -f - << 'EOF'
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: cpu-throttle
spec:
  containers:
  - name: stress
    image: progrium/stress
        command: ['stress', '--cpu', '1', '--timeout', '60s']
    resources:
      requests:
        cpu: 100m
      limits:
        cpu: 200m
EOF

# Attendi qualche secondo
sleep 5
kubectl top pod cpu-throttle

exercises.task:
1. Crea un ConfigMap con configurazione dell'app
2. Crea un Pod con due container
3. Entrambi accedono al ConfigMap montato
4. Verifica che vedano la stessa configurazione
hints: Un volume può essere montato in più container
I container condividono lo stesso filesystem montato
exercises.solution:
kubectl create configmap shared-config --from-literal=CONFIG_FILE=/app/config.yaml --from-literal=LOG_LEVEL=debug

kubectl apply -f - << 'EOF'
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: multi-container
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: busybox
    command: ['sh', '-c', 'while true; do cat /etc/config/CONFIG_FILE; sleep 5; done']
    volumeMounts:
    - name: config
      mountPath: /etc/config
  - name: sidecar
    image: busybox
    command: ['sh', '-c', 'while true; do cat /etc/config/LOG_LEVEL; sleep 5; done']
    volumeMounts:
    - name: config
      mountPath: /etc/config
  volumes:
  - name: config
    configMap:
      name: shared-config
EOF

kubectl exec multi-container -c app -- cat /etc/config/LOG_LEVEL
kubectl exec multi-container -c sidecar -- cat /etc/config/LOG_LEVEL

exercises.task:
1. Crea un Pod con solo requests (no limits) → Burstable
2. Crea un Pod con requests == limits → Guaranteed
3. Crea un Pod senza resources → BestEffort
4. Verifica la QoS class di ogni Pod
hints: Guaranteed = requests == limits per tutte le risorse
exercises.solution:
# Burstable: requests senza limits
kubectl run burstable --image=nginx --requests='cpu=100m,memory=128Mi'

# Guaranteed: requests == limits
kubectl run guaranteed --image=nginx --requests='cpu=100m,memory=128Mi' --limits='cpu=100m,memory=128Mi'

# BestEffort: nessuna risorsa
kubectl run besteffort --image=nginx

# Verifica QoS
kubectl get pod burstable -o jsonpath='{.status.qosClass}' && echo
kubectl get pod guaranteed -o jsonpath='{.status.qosClass}' && echo
kubectl get pod besteffort -o jsonpath='{.status.qosClass}' && echo
